answer: A sybil-resistant economy can pay graders via peer prediction: each agent scores others and is rewarded for matching the honest majority verdict and penalizing divergence. Lazy or copied votes fail to track the panel, so a colluding cluster of fake identities whose votes echo one leader earns a negative delta against consensus and loses money on every task. Graders also stake collateral in a vault escrow, forfeited if accuracy falls below the panel median, so each fake identity costs real capital up front plus recurring losses, making mass identity creation strictly unprofitable over time.
